pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church Primary School - Parent Partnership
pageCache.text:
Parent Partnership
The school values it's close relationship with parents and appreciates the importance of this integral partnership. We offer an Open Door Policy and there are many opportunities for parents to meet with Senior Leaders and teachers to discuss their children's needs and education.
In addition to this we have set up a Parent Partnership Group which comprises of a parent representative from each class. This group meets with the head teacher termly to discuss school related issues and suggest ideas and ways to improve the children's learning environment. It is a collaborative partnership and enables both parents and school to seek views, listen to ideas and work together to ensure the needs of the children and their families are met. It promotes our vision and provides a caring partnership supporting our children to "flourish",
Agenda items are requested before the meetings and minutes are made available to all parents via the class representative.

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church Primary School - Wrap-around Care: Breakfast and After School Club
pageCache.text:
wrap-around care
Breakfast Club
Everyone is welcome at Christ Church Primary School’s Breakfast Club which provides quality childcare for children from Nursery to Year 6. It is operated by our own staff, not a private company, and this ensures that the children know the staff well and they know the children. We provide a nutritious breakfast and prepare your child for the school day.
Opening times: The club is open every weekday during term time from 7.45 – 8.45 am. Your child can join at any time during this hour. Breakfast is served until 8.30 am.
Cost: The cost for children in YR-Y6 per day is £6.00. The cost for Nursery children is £10, as the staff pupil ratio for pre-school children is higher. Attendance by Nursery children needs to be booked in advance by contacting the school office.
Food provided: A selection of healthy cereals with semi-skimmed milk, brown and white toast with jam, butter and honey, orange or apple juice, yoghurt and fresh fruits.
Friday special menu!: The children enjoy and look forward to our Friday special menu which offers warm waffles, pancakes, or ham/cheese toasties and hot chocolate!
Activities: After breakfast, children enjoy a variety of activities such as table football, games, colouring, crafts and Lego. They also have the opportunity to play outside in the garden and playground. Children end the session with a prayer together before they walk into their classrooms to start the day.
Nursery and Reception children are accompanied to class by an adult.
Our After School Club provides a quality childcare facility for children from Reception to Year 6. The club runs from 3.30-6pm, Monday- Friday, during term time and is able to accommodate weekly, daily or occasional attendance.
We provide a drink and a healthy snack when the children arrive at 3.30 pm, followed by a ” pre- supper” snack at 5 pm . Please inform us of any allergies your child might have at time of booking. All children will be encouraged to join in a choice of activities including board games, arts and crafts and outdoor play.
Sessions run from 3.30-4.30pm, 4.30-5.45pm and 5.45-6pm, your child can be collected at any time between these times. Please be aware that late collection will incur an additional charge.
If you would like a place for your child, please complete the registration form in advance and let the school office know.
Your child does not have to attend every day, simply book the days you require.
The cost is £10.00 per day for the 3.30-5.45pm session, £4.50 for the 3.30-4.30pm session, £5.50 for the 4.30-5.45pm.session and £3 for the 5.45-6pm session..
Payment is made via Parent Pay.
Childcare vouchers are also accepted.
We reserve the right to refuse further bookings if the full fee is not paid.
We are currently offering provision for our Nursery children at the request of parents until 5pm. This needs to be pre-booked and the cost is £20 per session. (3.30-5pm)
Christ Church, the LDBS and the local authority are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and all staff hold an enhanced DBS check. There are also First Aid trained staff on site at all times.
Extended Services Policy

Clubs
Opportunities for children to extend their learning beyond the classroom are very important; they enable children to flourish and achieve in activities beyond academic learning. We ensure that we offer a wide range of extra curricular activities to facilitate this.
We encourage our children to develop their interests and have hobbies and activities to pursue out of school. We ensure that they have the chance to become involved in clubs and extra- curricular activities whenever possible.
Clubs take place before school, during lunchtimes and after school. They are run by external agencies, some by school staff and our older children are also supported to run clubs for our younger children.
We have strong links with local secondary schools and their students often run clubs during the school day. QE Boys regularly visit us and run computer and maths clubs.
There are a variety of different clubs, including many sports, drama, art music and languages. If parents or children approach us, we will always look to investigate and introduce new clubs if they are financially viable.

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church Primary School - Art & DT
pageCache.text:
Art & DT
At Christ Church Primary School we provide students with the opportunity to explore their creativity in art lessons through a wide variety of mediums. Students are encouraged to persevere, take ownership of their artwork and create truly unique pieces of art.
We believe that the process of art work is more important than the end product. Children should have the opportunity to use art as a means of expressing their feelings towards the world and for translating how they see things within the environment using interesting and varied techniques and from a variety of starting points. The children are also given opportunities to lead their own artwork, make decisions about their art, be imaginative, consider improvements as well as actually being given the opportunity to improve a piece of art.
It is vital to show the children that their work is valued and this is done by providing an audience and purpose for work, displaying around the school as well as in the classroom.
Art is celebrated throughout the school year and receives particular attention during Arts Week when the school sets out a gallery and invites parents and the local community to visit and enjoy the art work. Service.
Our children produce creative work, exploring their ideas and recording their experiences. They become proficient in drawing, painting, sculpture and other art, craft and design techniques. They can evaluate and analyse their work. They know about great artists, craft makers and designers, and understand the historical and cultural development of their art forms.

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church Primary School - Personal, Social and Health Education
pageCache.text:
Personal, Social and Health Education
At Christ Church, we understand the importance of providing an education which gives children the knowledge, skills, and attributes they need to keep themselves healthy and safe and to prepare them for life and work in modern Britain.
Our PSHE provision helps our children to achieve their academic potential, and leave school equipped with skills they will need throughout later life. Through PSHE, we help pupils to manage many of the most critical opportunities, challenges and responsibilities they will face growing up.
At Christ Church we have adopted Jigsaw, the mindful approach to PSHE/HWB, which brings together Personal, Social, Health Education, emotional literacy, social skills and spiritual development in a comprehensive scheme of learning. This links well with our School Vision enabling every child to flourish in all aspects of their development. Our school values of trust, compassion, respect, wisdom, perseverance and service are embedded well throughout and provide a thread on which to base our learning.
Children are taught a lesson a week where teachers focus on tailoring the lessons to their children’s needs and to enjoy building the relationship with their class, getting to know them better as unique human beings.
Teaching strategies are varied and are mindful of preferred learning styles and the need for differentiation. Our curriculum is designed as a whole school approach, with all year groups working on the same theme (Puzzle) at the same time. There are six themes throughout the year. Each theme begins with an introductory assembly, generating a whole school focus for adults and children alike.
For more information, please see the attached policy and curriculum overview.

Music
Music washes away from the soul, the dust of everyday life.
Music is a universal language that everyone can participate in and enjoy and during their time at Christ Church the children are all encouraged to explore music through a variety of avenues.
Music is taught in accordance with the National Curriculum and a specialist teacher ensures that all children have the opportunity to develop musical talents and abilities. During weekly lessons they learn to sing and to play tuned and untuned instruments with increasing accuracy, control and expression, to improvise and compose music, to use and understand notation and to perform, both solo and as part of an ensemble. They listen to both recorded and live music from a wide range of genres and find out about the history of music.
We use a music resource called Charanga and this is highly proficient in ensuring teachers are upskilled and have the resources at hand that they need to teach music well.
Children have the opportunity for whole class instrument tuition and the school has its own class sets of ukuleles, recorder and glockenspiels. This allows children to develop transferable music skills and musicianship. There are two school choirs.
We are part of B.E.A.T. ( Barnet Education Arts Trust) and this provides opportunities for our children to learn to play a variety of instruments with peripatetic staff. The children have the opportunity to learn a variety of instruments including drums, violin, cello, trumpet, clarinet and piano.
We value the importance of performance and encourage our children to share their skills regularly in assemblies as well as visits to the local community. Our musicians regularly perform at local residential homes and participate in termly evening recitals. The choir take part in Barnet School and LDBS events and have performed at The Royal Albert Hall with Year Six children embracing the wonderful opportunity to participate in Young Voices. This not only provides the children with enjoyable experiences that nurture confidence, social awareness and self esteem but also allows them the opportunity to practice our values of compassion, respect, trust and perseverance.
Music is everybody’s possession.
